description: Shows how supercooling, structural arrest, relaxation and thermal history produce amorphous glasses with distinct optical and mechanical properties.

related_resources.reason: Glass transitions and arrested noncrystalline structures.
Amorphous matter below its glass transition.
Manufacturing variations rather than room-temperature flow explain antique window thickness.
Time scales of glass viscosity and failure of medieval window flow explanation.
Lattices, Bragg diffraction, defects and crystalline structures.

historical_claims.anchor: Most ordinary window glass is an amorphous solid
At a glass transition, the disordered structure largely persists
historical_claims.source_locator: Structural arrest instead of equilibrium crystal melting.

historical_claims.anchor: Historic manufacturing processes produced panes with nonuniform thickness
historical_claims.source_locator: Windowpane thickness and negligible room-temperature flow.
